claim: Code models frequently exhibit poor alignment between predictive confidence and actual correctness, assigning high confidence to incorrect predictions and low confidence to correct ones.
stance_target: existence of a calibration gap in code LLMs motivating new work
quoted_support: these models frequently exhibit poor alignment between predictive confidence and actual correctness. In practice, they often assign high confidence to incorrect predictions and low confidence to correct ones which undermine their reliability.

claim: A post-hoc weighted logistic-scaling recalibration (Platt-scaling variant upweighting incorrect predictions) applied to internal uncertainty signals achieves over 90% selective accuracy at 80% coverage on MBPP+ for DeepSeek-Coder-7B and CodeLlama-7B.
stance_target: feasibility of post-hoc calibration + abstention for code
quoted_support: The method yields the lowest brier score and ECE scores among tested strategies, and at 80% coverage, achieves over 90% selective accuracy.

claim: No single uncertainty metric emerges as a task-agnostic solution for code calibration; effective abstention requires per-instance behavioral calibration rather than a single distributional metric.
stance_target: difficulty of a universal code confidence signal
scope_conditions: defect prediction, vulnerability detection, code generation
quoted_support: no single uncertainty metric emerges as a task-agnostic solution. This supports one of our key insights: effective abstention in code tasks requires behavioral calibration, i.e., alignment of internal confidence with correctness at the per-instance level.

claim: This is an early-stage/roadmap paper (~4.9k words) whose confidence mechanisms are internal signals plus abstention heads, not a trained verbalized confidence interface.
stance_target: claim that verbalized code-confidence training is already covered by this paper
quoted_support: The framework begins by extracting internal uncertainty signals from the model, serving as indicators of prediction confidence.
